newsitem.title: USA: Prices of popular breakfast cereals barely budge.
newsitem.headline: Prices of popular breakfast cereals barely budge.

text.p: Breakfast cereals are giving consumers more crunch for less cash but some of the biggest brand names have barely cut their prices, two congressmen announced Thursday.

In what has become an annual study of U.S. cereal prices, Democratic Reps. Charles Schumer of New York and Sam Gejdenson of Connecticut said consumers saved an estimated $448 million since manufacturers slashed prices last year.
The four biggest cereal makers -- General Mills Inc., Kellogg Co., Post and Quaker Oats Co. -- cut prices an average of between 11 percent and 20 percent last year.
"But our report also clearly shows that the American breakfast cereal industry is a long way from earning any 'consumer-friendly' medals," Gejdenson said.

Some of the most popular cereals such as Cheerios, Wheaties and Total had no price cuts, he said. And others like Rice Krispies, Healthy Choice and Special K trimmed prices but not to the extent of other brands by the same manufacturer.

"Our analysis shows that cereal prices actually fell by one-third of the average price reductions announced by major manufacturers," Gejdenson said. "Now more than ever, shoppers must watch this industry like a hawk."
Earlier this month, General Mills announced it would increase its cereal prices by about a dime a box.
A few weeks after the two congressmen issued their cereal price report last year, Post made the first in a series of industry price reductions.
